text: Casein is first formed into rods, tubes or sheets, and only then hardened: the shaped piece soaks in a formaldehyde bath that cross-links the protein into an insoluble, horn-like thermoset. Because the bath works from the outside in, the hardening is the long step.

steps.note: Colourants are mixed into the dry casein powder.
The casein is heated until it clumps together.
The casein is pressed into bars, which are pushed out again through a shaping opening, then pressed into blocks.

steps.name: harden
steps.note: The casein is soaked in about 5 % formalin, a formaldehyde solution, which hardens it from the outside in.
The galalith is dried slowly, so it does not crack or warp.
